minutes.headline: Superintendent Burnham announced her retirement at year's end; a search subcommittee was formed
minutes.summary: The committee heard that Superintendent Burnham will retire at the end of the school year and appointed a search subcommittee; it also reviewed a restructured athletic-fee proposal, a Turkey Hill fire-alarm and door/security bid, a transportation contract renegotiation, and feedback on the joint town-building design plan's placement of the ACE program in a basement space. No final decisions were made on the fee schedule, cell-phone policy, or the building design; those were deferred to future meetings.

what_happened.line: Superintendent Burnham announced her retirement at the end of the school year, and the committee appointed a two-member search subcommittee.
The committee took no vote on a restructured athletic fee proposal, choosing to gather public and booster feedback before deciding nearer the budget vote.
Dr. Gilson was authorized to negotiate and finalize a renegotiated transportation contract after an initial bid came in with a steep first-year increase.
The department will send the town's building design committee written objection to placing the ACE special education program in a basement-level space.
A phase-one door and security award was approved at Turkey Hill, with full door replacement deferred pending state (MSBA) guidance.

why_it_matters: A superintendent search will shape district leadership heading into next school year, and residents will see subcommittee updates as it proceeds.
The undecided athletic fee proposal will factor into the FY budget residents vote on, once public and booster feedback is gathered.
Where the ACE special education program is housed in the planned joint municipal building affects students and families relying on that program.
watch_next: January 21 MSBA superintendents' webinar, ahead of a decision on the remaining Turkey Hill door replacement
Cell phone policy discussion returning at the next meeting or the first meeting in February

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.coverage: official minutes are a summary only
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the outcome of every vote that appears in both, and on the handful of figures the official minutes bother to state (warrant total, donation amounts, the $300,000 Turkey Hill door capital, FY24 free cash), but the official minutes omit nearly all the numeric and procedural detail our caption-derived minutes captured — the withdrawn transportation motion, the ARPA transfer, and virtually every athletic-finance and revolving-account figure. The one thing a reader should actually check is the Vincent Joseph scholarship: our minutes give $115,000 (heard twice, at the vote and in the figures) against the official minutes' $15,000 — a $100,000 gap on the same named gift that is too large to be a digit-grouping slip.
